# Poker Arena

> A heads-up No-Limit Hold'em bot arena. Developers register a bot, the arena runs it 24/7 against other bots on permanent ring tables, and ranks it by bb/100. Bots are HTTPS webhooks: the arena POSTs the state of the hand, the bot answers with an action.

This file indexes everything an AI coding agent needs to write, test and deploy a bot.
Paths are relative to the repository root. All monetary amounts everywhere in this
system are integer chips, never floats and never big blinds: `1bb = 100` chips.

## Season 1 rules

- Game: heads-up No-Limit Texas Hold'em, exactly `2` players.
- Stacks: `100bb` = `10000` chips, **reset to 100bb at the start of every hand**.
- Blinds: SB `50` / BB `100` chips. No antes, no straddles.
- Position: **the button is the small blind**. It acts first preflop and last postflop.
- Rake: `5%` of the pot, capped at `60` chips (`0.6bb`), no flop no drop. Heads-up pots are small, so this cap binds often.
- Min-raise, side pots and showdown order follow standard rules (Robert's Rules).
- Ranking: bb/100 after rake. A bot must play `10000` hands on its current version to be listed (`2000` during the Season 1 beta).
- The arena pairs every active bot round-robin once a minute and plays a batch of hands; the button alternates each hand.
- Redeploying a bot resets its season stats.
- Action time limit: `5s` per action for webhook bots, plus a time bank that starts at `1s`, refills `500ms` per hand and caps at `10s`. The bank only pays for the part of a response that runs past the `5s` base, and it carries across hands. Redeploying or re-activating a bot resets it to `1s`.
- A late, invalid, or erroring response is coerced to **check if legal, otherwise fold**, and recorded with `"forced": true`. `20` consecutive transport failures (timeout, HTTP error, unparseable body) set the bot to `status: "error"` until it is redeployed; an illegal-but-parseable action is coerced without counting toward that.

## Live arena

- **Webhook bots are currently disabled.** `GET /api/season` returns
  `webhookBotsEnabled: false`; registering or deploying a webhook bot is rejected with `400`, and
  the arena makes no outbound requests at all. Only builtin-strategy bots compete for now.
  Check that field before telling a user to stand up a webhook.

- Base URL: `https://vcode-poker-arena.hiro15254.com` (`https://vcode-poker-arena.hiro15254.workers.dev` also works).
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`. Get a key with `POST /api/signup {"name":"..."}`.
- **Set a User-Agent.** The CDN in front of the arena blocks the default `Python-urllib/x.y`
  user agent with a `403` and an HTML body. `requests`, `curl`, `node-fetch` and Go's client
  are fine. The bundled Python client sets one for you.
- [Python API client](../sdk/python/poker_arena/client.py): `ArenaClient(api_key=...)` with
  `leaderboard()`, `my_bots()`, `bot(id)`, `hands(bot_id, limit)`, `hand(hand_id)`,
  `deploy(bot_id, webhook_url=...)`, `activate(id)`, `test_match(...)`. Stdlib only.

## Uploaded bots (not yet running)

- Sandbox execution is not built yet, but the acceptance rule is fixed and enforceable today:
  **one `.py` file, at most `8192` bytes of code**, where code bytes = UTF-8 bytes after removing
  `#` comments and blank lines. String literals — **including docstrings** — do count, so a range
  table cannot be smuggled into a docstring and parsed from `__doc__`. Write long prose in `#` comments.
  Whole-file raw size must stay under `256KB`.
- The point is to compete on logic, not on the size of a precomputed table.
- Check locally before submitting: `pnpm measure <bot.py>` or `python3 sdk/python/check_bot.py <bot.py>`.
  Both agree byte-for-byte with the server (`packages/protocol/src/upload.ts` is the source of truth,
  `sdk/python/poker_arena/upload.py` mirrors it).
- Live values are in `GET /api/season` under `upload`.

## Protocol

- [ActRequest JSON Schema](../packages/protocol/schema/act_request.schema.json): the body the arena POSTs to a bot. `pot` is every chip committed so far including the current street's bets; `players[].bet` is that seat's total for the current street; `actions[].amount` is always a street total, never an increment.
- [ActResponse JSON Schema](../packages/protocol/schema/act_response.schema.json): the bot's answer. `{"action":"fold"|"check"|"call"}` or `{"action":"raise","amount":N}` where `N` is the **raise to** total for the street. Out-of-range raises are invalid, not clamped.
- [Protocol types (TypeScript, source of truth)](../packages/protocol/src/index.ts): `ActRequest`, `ActResponse`, `PlayerState`, `ActionRecord`, `LegalAction`, `Street`, `CHIPS_PER_BB`.
- [Season config types](../packages/protocol/src/season.ts): `SeasonConfig`, rake and blind values for Season 1.

## Docs

- [REST API contract](API.md): every endpoint, the bot webhook contract, HMAC signing (`X-Arena-Signature: sha256=<hex>` over the raw body), and the error codes.
- [Bot development guide (Japanese)](BOT_DEVELOPMENT.md): how the arena works, the webhook contract with a full worked example, time limits, local testing, registration, and how to iterate on a bot with an AI agent using the hand-history API.
- [API types](../packages/protocol/src/api.ts): request/response types for bots, leaderboard, tables, hand histories and test matches.
- [Full specification (Japanese)](../SPEC.md): game rules (§2), bot execution modes (§4), time limits (§5), hand-history visibility (§6), protocol (§11).

## Python SDK

- [SDK README](../sdk/python/README.md): quickstart, the exact JSON of one ActRequest and one ActResponse, and the full API reference. Standard library only, Python 3.11+.
- [poker_arena/types.py](../sdk/python/poker_arena/types.py): TypedDicts mirroring the wire format, `CHIPS_PER_BB`, `to_bb()`, `to_chips()`, and the response constructors `fold() check() call() raise_to(n)`.
- [poker_arena/cards.py](../sdk/python/poker_arena/cards.py): card parsing (`"As"`, `"Td"`, `"7h"`) and a 5-/7-card hand evaluator returning an integer score where higher wins and equal ties. Handles the A-5 wheel.
- [poker_arena/bot.py](../sdk/python/poker_arena/bot.py): the `Bot` base class and the `Request` wrapper — `to_call`, `pot`, `can_check`, `can_raise`, `min_raise`, `max_raise`, `hero`, `villain`, `position`, `pot_odds`, `raise_to_pot_fraction(f)`.
- [poker_arena/server.py](../sdk/python/poker_arena/server.py): `serve(bot, port, secret)`, a dependency-free webhook server that verifies the HMAC signature and answers a crashing `act()` with a legal fallback instead of a 500.

## Examples

- [always_call.py](../sdk/python/examples/always_call.py): the minimal bot, for checking the plumbing.
- [tight_bot.py](../sdk/python/examples/tight_bot.py): a readable heads-up strategy — preflop ranges, c-betting, and hand-strength buckets, each marked as a place to plug in your own logic.
- [equity_bot.py](../sdk/python/examples/equity_bot.py): Monte Carlo equity against a random villain range compared against the pot odds, with a hard time budget.
- [test_evaluator.py](../sdk/python/tests/test_evaluator.py): the evaluator's test suite; runs under pytest or standalone with `python3 tests/test_evaluator.py`.

## Optional

- [Game engine](../packages/engine/src/engine.ts): the authoritative betting logic — what counts as a legal action, how `pot` and min-raises are computed, and how invalid responses are coerced.
- [Local simulator](../packages/simulator/src/cli.ts): `pnpm sim --hands 1000 --bots tight,call` plays built-in benchmark bots against each other on the same engine.
